title: Why Putin’s Defenders Are Increasingly American
gist: Karatnycky argues Putin's Western apologists are now mostly American and span the political spectrum, and are modern 'fellow travelers' who, like Stalin's admirers, embrace a brutal regime to attack domestic enemies. He says they are more culpable than their predecessors because they can delay aid to Ukraine, and that Trump has joined them by weakening Ukraine and lifting energy sanctions.

insights.claim: A Kremlin-linked 'International Club of National Unity' lists several Americans in its leadership, notably Columbia economist Jeffrey Sachs, who has promoted Kremlin lines that the 2014 Maidan was a US-backed coup.
insights.speaker: Adrian Karatnycky
insights.so_what: Reputational and information-operation risk around prominent Western academics aligned with Russian narratives.

insights.claim: Putin's Western sympathizers are now predominantly American and span the political spectrum, while parts of the European right such as Marine Le Pen have turned critical since the 2022 full-scale invasion.
insights.speaker: Adrian Karatnycky
insights.so_what: Russia-friendly sentiment is shifting toward US political and media figures, which matters for Ukraine aid politics.

insights.claim: American figures cited as Putin's fellow travelers include Candace Owens, the Tate brothers, John Mearsheimer, Tucker Carlson, Oliver Stone, Rep. Anna Paulina Luna, Steve Bannon, Michael Flynn and Rick Sanchez, who hosts a flagship program on RT from Moscow.
insights.speaker: Adrian Karatnycky
insights.so_what: The author's characterization of named individuals; their audiences amplify Kremlin narratives across US media.
insights.locator: At the annual St. Petersburg Economic Forum

insights.claim: After RT was shut down in the West, Russia moved influence operations to social media, boosting voices against the 'woke agenda' and spending millions on US influencers and podcasters, aided by Russian bot networks.
insights.speaker: Adrian Karatnycky
insights.so_what: Russian influence spending targets US right-wing audiences; a source of political and disinformation risk.
insights.locator: Following the shutdown of RT in the West

insights.claim: Putin's Decree 809 of November 2022 frames Russia as a traditional, faith-based patriarchal society against Western decadence, designed to win over the cultural right and aligned with the Russian Orthodox Church.
insights.speaker: Adrian Karatnycky
insights.so_what: Ideological outreach to Western social conservatives is state policy rather than coincidence.
insights.locator: As part of the effort to win over the cultural right

insights.claim: Alexander Dugin, tasked by Russian intelligence with wooing Western right-wing ideologues, has been platformed by Tucker Carlson and Alex Jones, helping spread the view of Russia as a haven from liberal ideology.
insights.speaker: Adrian Karatnycky
insights.so_what: Shows the pipeline from Russian intelligence-linked ideologues to US mass audiences.
insights.locator: The Kremlin's efforts to influence the U.S. right

insights.claim: The common thread among fellow travelers of Stalin, Hitler, Mussolini and North Vietnam is that domestic political or intellectual hatreds lead them to embrace brutal foreign regimes: the enemy of my domestic enemy is my friend.
insights.speaker: Adrian Karatnycky
insights.so_what: Useful model for predicting who amplifies hostile-state narratives: look at domestic grievance rather than foreign-policy analysis.
insights.quote: The enemy of my domestic enemy is my friend.
insights.locator: The through line that connects many of these fellow travelers

insights.claim: Today's Putin supporters are more culpable than Stalin's because evidence of Russian war crimes is abundant and, unlike in the 1930s, the West can stop Putin, while apologists can delay or cut off aid to Ukraine.
insights.speaker: Adrian Karatnycky
insights.so_what: Frames pro-Russia advocacy as having direct effects on Ukraine aid policy.
insights.locator: Stalin's crimes were an order of magnitude greater

insights.claim: Free-speech advocates among US pundits ignore Putin's censorship and the criminalization of disapproval of the 'special military operation'.
insights.speaker: Adrian Karatnycky
insights.so_what: Highlights a rhetorical inconsistency the author uses to question fellow travelers' sincerity.

themes.theme: Trump as the newest fellow traveler

insights.claim: Trump has crossed a geopolitical Rubicon by weakening Ukraine's ability to defend itself and lifting energy sanctions, giving the Kremlin financial resources to use against Ukraine while Russia tries to render its cities uninhabitable.
insights.speaker: Adrian Karatnycky
insights.so_what: Lifted energy sanctions help Russia's finances and could affect oil and gas markets; the author says Western and Republican backlash may force a reversal.
insights.locator: Yet no one will be judged more harshly
